After a year in stealth, foreign-made robot distributor RoboStore has launched a U.S.-based robotics manufacturing and systems-integration company called Robo Inc.

According to Robo Inc., the New York-based company plans to open a 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island that is expected to be fully operational by the first quarter of 2027. The company said the site will support engineering, software, integration, production, testing, service and customer support.

The public launch comes just two weeks after the U.S. banned new advanced foreign-made robotics. [...] Greg Bock

Insider Brief

 RoboStore has launched Robo Inc., a U.S.-based robotics manufacturing and systems-integration company, with plans to open a 66,000-square-foot Long Island facility by the first quarter of 2027.
 The launch comes shortly after new U.S. restrictions on advanced foreign-made robots, while Robo Inc. plans to emphasize U.S.-based assembly, localized data infrastructure, security reviews and application-specific integration.
 Robo Inc. will take a hardware-agnostic approach built on RoboStore’s experience selling and deploying more than 1,500 humanoid and quadruped robots to about 4,500 customers, including Harvard, MIT, Amazon and Nvidia. [...] The company noted that the new business builds on RoboStore’s experience distributing foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots in North America. RoboStore said it has sold and deployed more than 1,500 robots and served about 4,500 customers, including Harvard, MIT, Amazon and Nvidia. RoboStore is also an official distributor of China’s Unitree Robotics, in the news this week for its Shanghai IPO.

Rather than developing a single general-purpose robot, Robo Inc. will take a hardware-agnostic approach, selecting robot platforms and components based on the needs of individual applications. The company said it will focus on systems that can address defined operational problems with clear expectations for performance, safety and integration into existing workflows.

results.title: Facing Ban, US Seller of Chinese Robots Makes Domestic Manufacturing Push | PCMag
results.content:
New York-based RoboStore has been selling humanoid and dog-like robots from Chinese vendor Unitree. But on Monday, it launched Robo Incorporated, a US-based manufacturing and systems integration company.

“As the US races to strengthen domestic manufacturing and secure critical technologies, Robo Inc. will open a 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island, New York, which is expected to be fully operational by Q1 2027,” the company said.

PCMag logo

Although humanoid robots are an emerging market, you may have seen them on social media, at trade shows, or at company events. RoboStore notes that it’s sold and deployed “more than 1,500 humanoid and quadruped robots while serving 4,500 customers,” including Nvidia, Amazon, and Harvard University. [...] However, the newly launched Robo Inc. has more modest ambitions than other players seeking to build general-purpose humanoid robots that can serve as artificial butlers or factory workers. It's focused on “the most common customer need: a robotic solution that can be deployed against specific operational problems today, with realistic performance expectations, clear safety boundaries, and a plan for integration into existing workflows —not an all-in-one humanoid promised to handle every task.” [...] “Importantly, the company is designing security and safety checkpoints into its integration process, including reviews of data flows, network access, software controls, operating environments, and application-specific risks,” the company says. “Robo Inc. draws on patterns seen across thousands of purchases, deployments, repairs, and integration requests from customers.”

By The Robot Report Staff |

RoboStore has provided Unitree robots to more than 4,000 U.S. customers.

RoboStore has provided Unitree robots to more than 4,000 U.S. customers. Source: RoboStore

As labor and competitive pressures mount, more companies are looking to localize robotics production and adoption. RoboStore, a leading distributor of foreign humanoid and quadruped robots in North America, today publicly launched Robo Inc., a U.S.-based robotics manufacturer and systems integrator. [...] After a year in stealth, Robo Inc. builds on RoboStore’s experience with selling and deploying more than 1,500 humanoid and quadruped robots and serving 4,500 customers in North America, said RoboStore. It intends to combine global supply chains with U.S.-based engineering, software, integration, production, testing, service, and support.

Just as Western companies set up subsidiaries and affiliates in China to gain entry to that market, Robo Inc. could be part of a similar trend, with foreign businesses launching spinoffs to maintain access to the U.S. market in the face of growing trade restrictions.

results.title: Robo Inc. Launches US Humanoid Robot Integrator; China Spy Law Still Follows Hardware
results.content:
Roboinc.com

RoboStore, North America's most active distributor of humanoid and quadruped robots, today publicly launched Robo Inc., a US-based manufacturing and systems integration company designed to fill the compliance gap left by the Federal Communications Commission's July 28 decision to block new Chinese-made advanced robots from the American market. The company says it will open a 66,000-square-foot (roughly 6,130 square meters) facility on Long Island, New York, expected to be operational by January 2027 — a concrete deadline and a named address in a sector that has historically offered neither. [...] ### What Comes Next

The 66,000-square-foot (6,130 square meters) Long Island facility is planned to begin producing US-localized robotic solutions in January 2027. Between now and then, Robo Inc. will need to hire domestic engineering talent, establish supplier relationships, secure necessary certifications, and demonstrate to prospective customers that its security review process is rigorous enough to satisfy both corporate IT teams and, for those customers who need it, regulatory requirements. [...] RoboStore distributes foreign-made robots — including Unitree platforms — to American customers. Robo Inc. adds US-based assembly, software integration, security hardening, and testing to that supply chain, creating a "global-to-local" model in which the hardware may still come from foreign (including Chinese) manufacturers, but the integration work — security review of data flows, network access, software controls, and application-specific risks — happens on US soil under American engineering oversight. The planned Long Island facility will be the physical location where that integration work occurs, beginning in January 2027.

results.content:
RoboStore already provides custom software development for specific applications. Robo Inc. is expected to extend this type of work through U.S.-based manufacturing, testing, and integration.

## A 66,000-Square-Foot Facility Takes Shape

A major part of the Robo Inc. strategy is a planned 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island, New York. The site is expected to begin operations during the first quarter of 2027.

The facility is planned to support manufacturing, engineering, systems integration, testing, service, and related activities. As a result, it could give the company a dedicated location for preparing systems before they are deployed to customers. [...] Successful U.S. robotics deployment can depend on integration, testing, security, training, maintenance, and long-term support. Robo Inc. is positioning itself around those areas while also developing a U.S. manufacturing base.

With the Long Island facility expected to begin operations in 2027, the company's next stage will show how effectively this model can connect imported platforms, U.S. engineering, and practical workplace applications.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### 1. What is Robo Inc.?

Robo Inc. is a U.S.-based robotics company launched by RoboStore. It focuses on manufacturing, systems integration, testing, deployment, and support for organizations using robot platforms.

### 2. What does Robo Inc. do? [...] ## RoboStore Builds a New Path for Robot Deployment

RoboStore has already built experience as a North American distributor and technology partner for Unitree platforms. Its offerings include humanoid and quadruped robots, technical support, training, and custom solutions.

The new company was introduced publicly on August 10, 2026, after operating in stealth for about a year. As reported by The Robot Report, Robo Inc. is being positioned as a New York-based manufacturer and integrator that will support U.S. organizations with local engineering, integration, testing, and deployment services.
